Original text: Fork the main Sphinx repository (sphinx-doc/sphinx) using the GitHub interface.
Atomic rule: Fork the sphinx-doc/sphinx repository on GitHub before making changes.
Section context: "The recommended way for new contributors to submit code to Sphinx is to fork this repository and submit a pull request after committing changes to their fork." The fork is the stated entry point for the whole submission chain.
Notes: Step 2 of the numbered Getting started sequence.

Original text: Clone the forked repository to your machine.
Atomic rule: Clone your own fork locally and work in that clone.
Section context: Step follows directly from the fork step; the section offers no alternative to working from a personal fork.
Notes: Step 3 of the numbered Getting started sequence.

Original text: Create a new working branch. Choose any name you like.
Atomic rule: Create a new working branch for the change instead of committing on master.
Section context: "Choose any name you like." The section places no constraint on the branch name, only on the existence of a separate branch.
Notes: Step 5 of the numbered Getting started sequence. Contrast with SymPy, which constrains the branch name.

Original text: Write your code along with tests that shows that the bug was fixed or that the feature works as expected.
Atomic rule: Include tests demonstrating the bug fix or the new feature alongside the code change.
Section context: Step 6 ("Hack, hack, hack.") states code and tests as a single deliverable; no exception is offered for either bug fixes or features.
Notes: Broadest of the three test-inclusion statements on this page; see also C019 and C026.

Original text: Add a bullet point to CHANGES.rst if the fix or feature is not trivial (small doc updates, typo fixes), then commit
Atomic rule: Add a bullet point to CHANGES.rst for any change that is not trivial.
Section context: The parenthesis enumerates what counts as trivial ("small doc updates, typo fixes"), so the exemption is closed rather than open-ended.
Notes: Strictest and most precisely scoped of the three CHANGES.rst statements; see C012 and C054.

Original text: Push changes in the branch to your forked repository on GitHub:
Atomic rule: Push the working branch to your GitHub fork.
Section context: Step 8; presupposes the fork created in step 2 and the branch created in step 5.
Notes: Step 8 of the numbered Getting started sequence.

Original text: Submit a pull request from your branch to the master branch.
Atomic rule: Open the pull request against the master branch.
Section context: Sphinx's default branch is master, not main; the instruction names the target branch exactly.
Notes: Step 9 of the numbered Getting started sequence.

Original text: GitHub recognizes certain phrases that can be used to automatically update the issue tracker. For example, including 'Closes #42' in the body of your pull request will close issue #42 if the PR is merged.
Atomic rule: Reference the issue being fixed with a closing keyword such as "Closes #42" in the pull request body.
Section context: Framed as what GitHub recognises rather than as a requirement; the page offers it as an example, not a mandated format.
Notes: Sphinx's analogue of SymPy's autoclose-syntax rules, but stated far more weakly.

Original text: The pull request will then need to be approved by one of the core developers before it is merged into the main repository.
Atomic rule: Obtain approval from a core developer before the pull request is merged.
Section context: Restated in step 10 of Getting started: "Wait for a core developer or contributor to review your changes."
Notes: Acceptance gate stated twice on the page; both statements name a second human.

Original text: You may be asked to address comments on the review. If so, please avoid force pushing to the branch.
Atomic rule: Do not force push to the pull request branch when addressing review comments.
Section context: "Sphinx uses the squash merge strategy when merging PRs, so follow-up commits will all be combined." The section states the reason the prohibition costs the contributor nothing.
Notes: Conditional on a review having happened. Compare Django C044, which states the same prohibition unhedged.

Original text: Try to use the same code style as used in the rest of the project.
Atomic rule: Match the code style already used in the rest of the project.
Section context: The section immediately delegates the mechanical part of style to ruff and mypy, leaving this bullet to cover only what the tools do not.
Notes: The only prose style rule on the page that is not delegated to a tool.

Original text: For non-trivial changes, please update the CHANGES.rst file.
Atomic rule: Update CHANGES.rst for non-trivial changes.
Section context: Repeats the Getting started step without its parenthesised definition of "trivial", so it is the vaguer of the two.
Notes: Same obligation as C005, stated a second time on the same page.

Original text: If your changes alter existing behavior, please document this.
Atomic rule: Document any change that alters existing behaviour.
Section context: Attached to the CHANGES.rst bullet, but names no file and no place where the documentation should go.
Notes: Trigger is "changes alter existing behavior", which the section does not define.

Original text: New features should be documented.
Atomic rule: Document every new feature that the change adds.
Section context: The two following sentences ("Include examples and use cases where appropriate. If possible, include a sample...") hedge the elaboration, not the core obligation to document.
Notes: Applies only if the change adds a new feature.

Original text: Include examples and use cases where appropriate.
Atomic rule: Include examples and use cases in the documentation for a new feature.
Section context: "where appropriate" is left entirely to the contributor; the page gives no test for appropriateness.
Notes: Elaboration of C014.

Original text: If possible, include a sample that is displayed in the generated output.
Atomic rule: Include a sample in the documentation that appears in the generated output.
Section context: "If possible" is an explicit escape hatch, and "displayed in the generated output" can only be confirmed by building and reading the docs.
Notes: Elaboration of C014.

Original text: When adding a new configuration variable, be sure to document it and update sphinx/cmd/quickstart.py if it's important enough.
Atomic rule: Document any new configuration variable in the configuration documentation.
Section context: The sentence links "document it" to doc/usage/configuration.rst via a :doc: reference, so the destination is named even though the prose does not spell it out.
Notes: Applies only if the change adds a new configuration variable. The "if it's important enough" hedge attaches to the quickstart.py clause only, split out as C018.

Original text: When adding a new configuration variable, be sure to document it and update sphinx/cmd/quickstart.py if it's important enough.
Atomic rule: Update sphinx/cmd/quickstart.py when adding an important new configuration variable.
Section context: "if it's important enough" is the contributor's call and the page gives no threshold.
Notes: Applies only if the change adds a new configuration variable. Second atom of the same sentence as C017.

Original text: Add appropriate unit tests.
Atomic rule: Add unit tests covering the change.
Section context: Bare bullet in a list whose other items are equally terse; the Unit tests section below is where the same obligation is spelled out.
Notes: Same obligation as C004, restated without the demonstration requirement.

Original text: Style and type checks can be run as follows: uv run ruff check / uv run ruff format / uv run mypy
Atomic rule: Ensure the change passes ruff's lint checks.
Section context: The identical three commands are the ruff/mypy jobs in .github/workflows/lint.yml, which runs on every push and pull request, and the tox lint environment carries the comment "If you update any of these commands, don't forget to update the equivalent GitHub Workflow step".
Notes: First of three atoms split from one code block; Original text is the shared source block. CI job: lint.yml "ruff" step "ruff check --output-format=github".

Original text: Style and type checks can be run as follows: uv run ruff check / uv run ruff format / uv run mypy
Atomic rule: Format the code with ruff format.
Section context: Same section context as C020; lint.yml runs "ruff format --diff", which fails the build on any unformatted file.
Notes: Second of three atoms split from one code block. Sphinx has no .pre-commit-config.yaml, so nothing rewrites files at commit time.

Original text: Style and type checks can be run as follows: uv run ruff check / uv run ruff format / uv run mypy
Atomic rule: Ensure the change type-checks cleanly under mypy.
Section context: Same section context as C020; lint.yml runs a dedicated mypy job, plus pyright and ty jobs the documentation does not mention.
Notes: Third of three atoms split from one code block. pyright and ty are CI-only and produce no rows, per the manifest's context-only treatment of workflow files.

Original text: To run Python unit tests, we recommend using tox, which provides a number of targets and allows testing against multiple different Python environments
Atomic rule: Run the Python unit tests locally before submitting the change.
Section context: The section immediately offers two documented alternatives: "You can also test by installing dependencies in your local environment: uv run pytest" and "Or with pip: python -m pip install . --group test; pytest".
Notes: The obligation is that the tests are run, not that tox is the runner.

Original text: To run JavaScript tests, use npm: npm install / npm run test
Atomic rule: Run the JavaScript test suite with npm when the change touches JavaScript.
Section context: A tip below notes "jasmine requires a Firefox binary to use as a test browser", which conditions the environment but not the obligation.
Notes: Applies only if the change adds or modifies JavaScript under sphinx/themes or tests/js.

Original text: New unit tests should be included in the tests/ directory where necessary
Atomic rule: Place new unit tests in the tests/ directory.
Section context: "where necessary" governs whether a new test is needed at all, not where it goes; the three bullets that follow all assume tests/ as the location.
Notes: Location rule; the sibling bullets C026 and C027 govern the content and the module.

Original text: For bug fixes, first add a test that fails without your changes and passes after they are applied.
Atomic rule: For a bug fix, add a test that fails before the patch is applied and passes after it.
Section context: Stated as an ordering requirement ("first add a test"), so the section asks for a demonstrated failure, not merely the presence of a test.
Notes: Applies only if the change is a bug fix. Distinct from C004: this one is only satisfiable by running the test twice.

Original text: Tests that need a sphinx-build run should be integrated in one of the existing test modules if possible.
Atomic rule: Add tests that require a sphinx-build run to an existing test module.
Section context: "if possible" is an explicit permission to create a new module where integration does not work.
Notes: Applies only if the new test needs a sphinx-build run.

Original text: Tests should be quick and only test the relevant components, as we aim that the test suite should not take more than a minute to run.
Atomic rule: Keep new tests fast and narrowly scoped.
Section context: The one-minute figure is stated as a project aim for the whole suite ("we aim that"), not as a budget for an individual test.
Notes: No per-test threshold is given, so the numeric limit cannot be attributed to any one contribution.

Original text: In general, avoid using the app fixture and app.build() unless a full integration test is required.
Atomic rule: Avoid the app fixture and app.build() in new tests.
Section context: Doubly hedged: "In general" and "unless a full integration test is required" both licence deviation, and the section does not say what makes a test a full integration test.
Notes: Names two exact tokens but attaches an open exception to both.

Original text: Contributing to documentation involves modifying the source files found in the doc/ folder.
Atomic rule: Make documentation changes in the source files under doc/.
Section context: Sphinx's own documentation is built from doc/ by the tox docs environment and by .github/workflows/builddoc.yml, so the folder is the only source of the published docs.
Notes: Locational conformance obligation extracted once from a descriptive sentence.

Original text: To build the documentation, run the following command: sphinx-build -M html ./doc ./build/sphinx --fail-on-warning
Atomic rule: Build the documentation with sphinx-build using --fail-on-warning.
Section context: The same --fail-on-warning invocation is the tox docs environment and the builddoc.yml CI job, so a warning is a build failure rather than a note.
Notes: Applies only if the contributor chooses to build the documentation. sphinx-autobuild is offered below as a preview alternative, not as a substitute for the checked build.

Original text: We do not accept pull requests altering the translation files directly. Instead, please contribute translations via the Transifex platform.
Atomic rule: Do not modify the gettext translation files directly in a pull request.
Section context: "Translated strings from the platform are pulled into the Sphinx repository by a maintainer before a new release." The section names the sanctioned alternative route, so the prohibition is absolute rather than a preference.
Notes: Covers sphinx/locale/**/*.po and sphinx/locale/sphinx.pot.

Original text: JavaScript stemming algorithms in sphinx/search/non-minified-js/*.js and stopword files in sphinx/search/_stopwords/ are generated from the Snowball project by running utils/generate_snowball.py.
Atomic rule: Regenerate the search stemmers and stopword files with utils/generate_snowball.py rather than editing them by hand.
Section context: The whole section is titled "Updating generated files" and exists to say which files must not be hand-edited.
Notes: Applies only if the change touches sphinx/search/non-minified-js/ or sphinx/search/_stopwords/. Conformance obligation extracted once, not one row per generated file.

Original text: Minified files in sphinx/search/minified-js/*.js are generated from non-minified ones using uglifyjs (installed via npm).
Atomic rule: Regenerate the minified search JavaScript from the non-minified sources with uglifyjs.
Section context: "See sphinx/search/minified-js/README.rst." The section points at a repository file for the exact invocation; that file was not fetched and produces no rows.
Notes: Applies only if the change touches sphinx/search/minified-js/ or its non-minified sources.

Original text: The searchindex.js files found in the tests/js/fixtures/* directories are generated by using the standard Sphinx HTML builder on the corresponding input projects found in tests/js/roots/* ... and can be regenerated by running the utils/generate_js_fixtures.py script.
Atomic rule: Regenerate the tests/js/fixtures searchindex.js files with utils/generate_js_fixtures.py.
Section context: "The fixtures provide test data used by the Sphinx JavaScript unit tests" — the section explains that hand-edited fixtures would silently invalidate the JS tests.
Notes: Applies only if the change touches tests/js/roots/ or tests/js/fixtures/.

Original text: You are responsible for any code you submit to Sphinx's repositories, regardless of whether it was manually written or generated by AI.
Atomic rule: Take responsibility for all submitted code whether written by hand or generated by AI.
Section context: Opening sentence of the policy; the two sentences that follow convert it into the concrete obligations C037 and C039.
Notes: Framing statement for the Responsibility section.

Original text: You must understand and be able to explain the code you submit as well as the existing related code.
Atomic rule: Understand and be able to explain the submitted code and the surrounding existing code.
Section context: Extended beyond the diff to "the existing related code", so the obligation is about the contributor's grasp of the codebase, not about anything in the patch.
Notes: Phrased as a capability of the submitter rather than a property of the artifact.

Original text: It is not acceptable to submit a patch that you cannot understand and explain yourself.
Atomic rule: Do not submit a patch you cannot understand and explain yourself.
Section context: Immediately follows C037 and restates it as a prohibition; no new condition is introduced.
Notes: Negative restatement of C037 in the same paragraph.

Original text: In explaining your contribution, do not use AI to automatically generate comments, pull request descriptions, or issue descriptions.
Atomic rule: Do not use AI to automatically generate code comments.
Section context: The prohibition is unqualified and sits in the Responsibility section, whose premise is that explanation must come from the contributor.
Notes: First atom of a three-target prohibition; the comments target lands inside the diff, unlike the other two.

Original text: In explaining your contribution, do not use AI to automatically generate comments, pull request descriptions, or issue descriptions.
Atomic rule: Do not use AI to automatically generate pull request or issue descriptions.
Section context: Same sentence as C039; these two targets are prose objects that live on GitHub rather than in the repository.
Notes: Second atom of the same sentence as C039.

Original text: You must disclose whether AI has been used to assist in the development of your pull request.
Atomic rule: Disclose whether AI was used in developing the pull request.
Section context: "We will reject any pull request that does not include the disclosure." The section states the consequence outright, making disclosure a condition of acceptance.
Notes: The PR template reserves a dedicated "AI Disclosure" heading for this.

Original text: If so, you must document which tool(s) have been used, how they were used, and specify what code or text is AI generated.
Atomic rule: Document which AI tools were used and how they were used.
Section context: Same rejection consequence as C041 applies; the section gives no minimal form for the disclosure beyond the three required facts.
Notes: First atom of a bundled three-part disclosure requirement. Applies only where AI was used.

Original text: If so, you must document which tool(s) have been used, how they were used, and specify what code or text is AI generated.
Atomic rule: Specify which code or text in the contribution is AI generated.
Section context: Same sentence as C042; this atom asks for a mapping onto the diff rather than a statement about tooling.
Notes: Second atom of the same sentence as C042. Applies only where AI was used.

Original text: Contributors are expected to submit code that meets Sphinx's standards.
Atomic rule: Submit code that meets Sphinx's quality standards.
Section context: The section names no standard and points to no style guide; the concrete standards live on the contributing page as ruff, mypy and the test rules.
Notes: Umbrella statement for the Code Quality section.

Original text: We will reject pull requests that we deem to be "AI slop".
Atomic rule: Do not submit pull requests that maintainers would judge to be AI slop.
Section context: "we deem" places the determination with the maintainers, and the term is defined only by an external Wikipedia link.
Notes: The rejection criterion is explicitly a maintainer judgement.

Original text: Do not waste developers' time by submitting code that is fully or mostly generated by AI, and doesn't meet our standards.
Atomic rule: Do not submit code that is mostly AI generated and below Sphinx's standards.
Section context: The prohibition is a conjunction: AI-generated *and* substandard. AI generation alone is not forbidden anywhere in the policy.
Notes: Both conjuncts must hold; the second is the same undefined standard as C044.

Original text: That means contributors must own the copyright of any code submitted to Sphinx or must include the BSD two clause compatible open source license(s) associated with the submitted code in the patch.
Atomic rule: Own the copyright of submitted code, or include a BSD-2-clause-compatible licence for it in the patch.
Section context: "All code in Sphinx is released under the two clause BSD copyright license." The disjunction gives a contributor who does not own the code a documented way to comply.
Notes: Applies only where the contributor does not own the copyright of some submitted code, which is a fact about provenance rather than about the patch.

Original text: Code generated by AI may infringe on copyright and it is the submitter's responsibility to not infringe.
Atomic rule: Ensure AI-generated code in the contribution does not infringe copyright.
Section context: "We reserve the right to reject any pull requests, AI-generated or not, where the copyright is in question." The section states a consequence but offers no way to establish non-infringement.
Notes: Infringement cannot be determined from the patch.

Original text: When interacting with developers (forums, discussions, issues, pull requests, etc.) do not use AI to speak for you, except for translation or grammar editing.
Atomic rule: Do not use AI to write your communications with developers, except for translation or grammar editing.
Section context: "Human-to-human communication is essential for an open source community to thrive." The exception for translation and grammar editing is written into the rule itself.
Notes: All four named venues are GitHub or forum surfaces.

Original text: The use of an AI agent that writes code and then submits a pull request autonomously is not permitted.
Atomic rule: Do not let an AI agent write code and open a pull request autonomously.
Section context: Unconditional, with its own heading; the following sentence supplies the required alternative rather than an exception.
Notes: The prohibition targets the autonomous write-and-submit sequence, not the use of AI as such.

Original text: A human must check any generated code and submit a pull request according to the 'Responsibility' section above.
Atomic rule: Have a human review the generated code and submit the pull request.
Section context: Immediately follows C050 as its positive counterpart, and cross-references the Responsibility section.
Notes: Requires a human actor in the submission chain.

Original text: A description of the purpose of this pull request. Ensure that all relevant information is included for reviewers, including any environment-specific details.
Atomic rule: Describe the purpose of the pull request and include the information reviewers need.
Section context: HTML comment under the "## Purpose" heading of the template; comments are stripped from GitHub's rendered view.
Notes: Extracted from the raw template file, not the rendered view.

Original text: If you plan to add tests or documentation after opening this PR, please note it here.
Atomic rule: Note in the pull request when tests or documentation are still to come.
Section context: Bullet inside the same Purpose HTML comment; conditional on the contribution being incomplete at opening time.
Notes: Applies only if tests or docs are deferred past PR opening.

Original text: For user-visible changes, remember to add an entry to CHANGES.rst.
Atomic rule: Add a CHANGES.rst entry for user-visible changes.
Section context: The template's trigger is "user-visible", where the contributing page's trigger is "not trivial"; neither document reconciles the two.
Notes: Third statement of the CHANGES.rst obligation; see C005 and C012.

Original text: Please add your name to AUTHORS.rst if you haven't already!
Atomic rule: Add your name to AUTHORS.rst if it is not already there.
Section context: Bullet inside the Purpose HTML comment; the condition "if you haven't already" is about the contributor's history, not the change.
Notes: Applies only if the contributor is not already listed in AUTHORS.rst.

Original text: Please add any relevant links here, especially including any GitHub issues or Pull Requests that this PR would resolve.
Atomic rule: Link the GitHub issues or pull requests the change resolves in the References section.
Section context: "This helps to ensure that reviewers have context from previous discussions or decisions." The template supplies three empty bullet placeholders for the links.
Notes: Template section with placeholder bullets "- <...>".

Original text: If AI was used in the preparation of this pull request, please disclose the tool(s) used, how they were used, and specify what code or text is AI generated.
Atomic rule: Disclose the AI tools used, how they were used, and what is AI generated.
Section context: "Please read our policy on AI generated code: https://www.sphinx-doc.org/en/master/internals/ai-policy.html" The template defers to the policy page for the binding wording.
Notes: Restates the Disclosure section of the AI policy inside the template.

Original text: If no AI tools were used, please write "No AI tools used" in this section.
Atomic rule: Write "No AI tools used" in the AI Disclosure section when no AI tools were used.
Section context: Supplies the exact string for the negative case, which the policy page does not.
Notes: Applies only where no AI tool was used; the positive case is C057.

Original text: In particular, all interaction is to be done by humans, including submission of pull requests.
Atomic rule: Have humans perform all project interaction, including submitting the pull request.
Section context: Final line of the template's AI Disclosure comment, generalising the policy page's AI Agents section.
Notes: Same obligation as C050, stated more broadly and more weakly.

Original text: As the deprecation policy describes, the first release of Sphinx that deprecates a feature (A.B) should raise a RemovedInSphinxXXWarning (where XX is the Sphinx version where the feature will be removed) when the deprecated feature is invoked.
Atomic rule: Raise a RemovedInSphinxXXWarning when a newly deprecated feature is invoked.
Section context: The parenthesis fixes the naming scheme exactly, and the deprecation policy section below fixes which version XX must name.
Notes: Applies only if the change deprecates a feature.

Original text: Thus, when adding a RemovedInSphinxXXWarning you need to eliminate or silence any warnings generated when running the tests.
Atomic rule: Eliminate or silence the deprecation warnings a new RemovedInSphinxXXWarning raises in the test suite.
Section context: "Assuming we have good test coverage, these warnings are converted to errors when running the test suite with warnings enabled: pytest -Wall", and tox sets PYTHONWARNINGS = error for every test environment.
Notes: Applies only if the change adds a RemovedInSphinxXXWarning. Directly comparable to Django C082.

Original text: If a feature is deprecated in a release A.x, it will continue to work in all A.x.x versions (for all versions of x). It will continue to work in all B.x.x versions but raise deprecation warnings. Deprecated features will be removed at the C.0.0.
Atomic rule: Do not remove a deprecated feature before the second major release after its deprecation.
Section context: "It means the deprecated feature will work during 2 MAJOR releases at least." The section restates the span as an explicit minimum.
Notes: Applies only if the change removes a deprecated feature. Stated descriptively; the contributor-facing obligation is the removal window.
